We need retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., single reaction) to target SMILES COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. Leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $405. We don't have price data, but we can assume typical small molecules are buyable. Need to find a template that can produce target from simple precursors that are buyable.

We have template 1914385 which seems to split the ester into methyl ester and a diene fragment? Let's examine: product is our target? The product_smiles in template 1914385 is '[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C@:5]12[CH2:6][CH:7]=[CH:8][CH2:9][C@H:10]1[C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]2' which matches our target (methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone). Yes.

The reactant_smiles are '[CH2:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH2:9].[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1' i.e., two fragments: a diene (butadiene?) and a methyl ester of a cyclohexenone? Actually second fragment is methyl ester of a cyclohexenone? Let's decode: CH3O-C(=O)-C1=CH- C(=O)-CH2-1? That's methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate? Not sure.

We need to check if those fragments are buyable. Use is_buyable on each.
